name: Amendments by the committee responsible – separate vote
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the Union Civil Protection Mechanism and Union support for health emergency preparedness and response, and repealing Decision No 1313/2013/EU (Union Civil Protection Mechanism)
part_text: (6) The protection to be ensured under the Union Mechanism should cover people, the environment and biodiversity, property, including but not limited to housing, critical infrastructure, such as energy and transport or communications and space infrastructure, food systems and cultural heritage, against all kinds of natural and human-induced disasters. Reference to natural and human-induced disasters should be understood as referring to the consequences of all natural and human-induced hazards while taking into account the multiple and cumulative systemic impact of such hazards. This should include acts of terrorism and sabotage, technological, Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear threats (CBRN) or environmental disasters, climate change, biodiversity loss, marine and inland water pollution, soil contamination and erosion water supply disruptions and water resilience, hydrogeological instability, disruptions of critical infrastructure, essential services and supply chains, health emergencies, cross-border threats to health, and other undefined hybrid disasters or emergencies, occurring inside or outside the Union. Those risks should be addressed through an integrated approach, including the ‘Health in All Policies’ approach, thereby ensuring that the health implications of policies across sectors are systematically taken into account, and also through the One Health approach. Those disasters require cross-sectoral coordination in situations where other Union crisis management mechanisms are also applied, including transport, infrastructure and operations.
